newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-VAN GAAL TO QUIT AS AJAX COACH AT END-SEASON, SAYS ANP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VAN GAAL TO QUIT AS AJAX COACH AT END-SEASON, SAYS ANP.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam coach Louis Van Gaal, who took the Dutch side to the top of European football, said he would quit the club at the end of the season, the ANP news agency said on Thursday.
Van Gaal, 45, took over as coach from Leo Beenhakker in September 1991. He had previously been assistant coach and had been in charge of the youth team.

Van Gaal has led Ajax to the Dutch league title for the last three seasons and also won the European Champions' Cup in 1995, the UEFA Cup in 1992, the Dutch and European Super Cups and the World Club Cup. Last season Ajax failed to retain their European crown, losing to Juventus on penalties in Rome.
In 52 "international" games under Van Gaal, Ajax lost only six times.
ANP said that Van Gaal told a news conference that he had achieved all he could at Ajax and now wanted to test himself elsewhere.
"It's time now to spread my wings," he was quoted as saying.
Amsterdam-born Van Gaal joined Ajax in 1988.
A journeyman footballer, he played for Ajax, FC Antwerp in Belgium, Telstar Beverwijk, Sparta Rotterdam and AZ Alkmaar.
